question:
A 53-year-old woman with pre-diabetes visits the student osteopathic clinic due to tension headaches.
She regularly follows up with her primary care physician and takes no medications other than ibuprofen
as needed. On examination, she is alert, oriented, and has an obese body habitus. Palpation reveals a
small, tender area located on the superior right aspect of the spinous process of C2, while the
remainder of the exam is unremarkable. What is the correct setup for the most appropriate treatment
for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Position in slight extension, apply traction, rotate bilaterally with
no sidebending (B) Slightly flex the neck to the level of C2, add slight axial compression, sidebend to
the right, rotate to the left (C) Extend the neck off the table to 45°, sidebend and rotate to the right (D)
Flex neck to C2, apply posterior-anterior pressure, sidebend and rotate contralaterally (E) Extend the
neck 30°, add traction, sidebend to the left and rotate to the right (F) Flex the neck to C3, apply lateral
compression, sidebend and rotate ipsilaterally (G) Slightly flex the neck just to the level of C2, sidebend
and rotate to the right (H) Maintain neutral neck position, apply axial compression, sidebend and rotate
bilaterally (I) Slightly extend the neck, add slight axial compression, slightly sidebend and rotate to the
left (J) Maintain neutral position, apply gentle traction, sidebend left and rotate right
 A. Position in slight extension, apply traction, rotate bilaterally with no sidebending
B. Extend the neck 30°, add traction, sidebend to the left and rotate to the right
C. Slightly extend the neck, add slight axial compression, slightly sidebend and rotate to the left
D. Maintain neutral neck position, apply axial compression, sidebend and rotate bilaterally
E. Flex neck to C2, apply posterior-anterior pressure, sidebend and rotate contralaterally
F. Extend the neck off the table to 45°, sidebend and rotate to the right
G. Maintain neutral position, apply gentle traction, sidebend left and rotate right
H. Slightly flex the neck just to the level of C2, sidebend and rotate to the right
I. Flex the neck to C3, apply lateral compression, sidebend and rotate ipsilaterally
J. Slightly flex the neck to the level of C2, add slight axial compression, sidebend to the right, rotate
to the left
